beats.title: switch to scheduled
beats.screen_note: (web) open a process for edit; in the launch mode segmented control, switch from "always on" to "scheduled" — labels are lowercase on screen. An inline schedule section + a week-summary bar appear in the dialog. (From a process row on the card, the same is reached via the schedule gear.)

direction.SCREEN: (web) open a process for edit; in the launch mode segmented control, switch from "always on" to "scheduled" — labels are lowercase on screen. An inline schedule section + a week-summary bar appear in the dialog. (From a process row on the card, the same is reached via the schedule gear.)
direction.NOTE: the gear flush at the end of the segmented control (aria-label "configure schedule", testid `process-dialog-configure-schedule`) opens the same section in EVERY launch mode — including "off" and "always on", where it just stores the windows for later ("saved with the process — switch to scheduled whenever you want these windows to run it"). Frame the gear while the mode still reads "always on" so that's visible, then flip to "scheduled".

beats.title: the schedule editor
beats.screen_note: (web) the "configure schedule" editor — day pills mon–sun, a time range with a start, "to", and stop using the time picker.

direction.SCREEN: (web) the "configure schedule" editor — day pills mon–sun, a time range with a start, "to", and stop using the time picker.
direction.NOTE: locate the card-row gear by icon (`button:has(svg.lucide-settings-2)`) — it has no accessible name.

beats.title: overnight windows
beats.screen_note: (web) set a range like 23:00 to 06:00; the "+1 day" badge and "ends the following day" note appear.

direction.SCREEN: (web) set a range like 23:00 to 06:00; the "+1 day" badge and "ends the following day" note appear.
direction.NOTE: the seeded admin preference is 12h and the default block ends 17:00, so a bare "06:00" parses as 6 pm. Type "6am" (or seed timeFormat 24h) or the frame will read 11pm→6pm and contradict the narration.

beats.title: presets
beats.screen_note: (web) the preset pills — "business hours", "extended hours", "weekday 24h", "24/7"; then the "new preset" save action.

direction.SCREEN: (web) the preset pills — "business hours", "extended hours", "weekday 24h", "24/7"; then the "new preset" save action.
direction.NOTE: dismiss the inline "new preset" form with its X cancel button, never Escape — Escape closes the whole dialog and "save schedule" disappears before b06 can click it.

beats.title: save it
beats.screen_note: (web) click "save schedule"; hold on the outside-window banner ("this looks outside the current window — a machine outside it will stop the process shortly after saving."), then the dialog closing back to the process row with its new schedule summary.

direction.SCREEN: (web) click "save schedule"; hold on the outside-window banner ("this looks outside the current window — a machine outside it will stop the process shortly after saving."), then the dialog closing back to the process row with its new schedule summary.
direction.NOTE: whose clock evaluates a window is a per-site setting now — `sites/{siteId}.schedulesFollowSiteTime`, with agent support since 3.2.3. It is three-state and absent is a real state: absent = never asked, `false` = declined, `true` = site time. Only `true` puts a `source="site"` timezone chip under the "configure schedule" title and swaps every schedule surface to "times run on the site's clock"; absent and `false` both read "times run on each machine's own clock". This scene records the flag OFF, so there is no chip to avoid and the machine-clock wording on camera is exactly what that site ships. The narration makes no timezone claim either way, so it stays true if a site later opts in — but do not re-film this episode against an opted-in site without re-cutting b04 and b06, or the chip and the "site's clock" wording sit on camera unspoken. The scene also pins the flag rather than leaving it absent so the one-time "which clock runs this site's schedules?" confirm banner stays off camera; teaching that banner is a scripted beat, not a side effect.

beats.title: the machine can edit them too
beats.screen_note: (native) the owlette desktop app on the machine — process detail, the schedule summary line, and the pencil beside the launch-mode control (aria-label "edit schedule", testid `edit-schedule`); open it to show the same day pills and time picker. Cut back to (web) the dashboard preset pills to land the contrast.

direction.SCREEN: (native) the owlette desktop app on the machine — process detail, the schedule summary line, and the pencil beside the launch-mode control (aria-label "edit schedule", testid `edit-schedule`); open it to show the same day pills and time picker. Cut back to (web) the dashboard preset pills to land the contrast.
direction.NOTE: this is the Tauri desktop app, not the retired python window — and it is NOT read-only. Assemble as a native insert in the editor.
